objects.definition:
enum zip_source_cmd {
    ZIP_SOURCE_OPEN,                /* prepare for reading */
    ZIP_SOURCE_READ,                /* read data */
    ZIP_SOURCE_CLOSE,               /* reading is done */
    ZIP_SOURCE_STAT,                /* get meta information */
    ZIP_SOURCE_ERROR,               /* get error information */
    ZIP_SOURCE_FREE,                /* cleanup and free resources */
    ZIP_SOURCE_SEEK,                /* set position for reading */
    ZIP_SOURCE_TELL,                /* get read position */
    ZIP_SOURCE_BEGIN_WRITE,         /* prepare for writing */
    ZIP_SOURCE_COMMIT_WRITE,        /* writing is done */
    ZIP_SOURCE_ROLLBACK_WRITE,      /* discard written changes */
    ZIP_SOURCE_WRITE,               /* write data */
    ZIP_SOURCE_SEEK_WRITE,          /* set position for writing */
    ZIP_SOURCE_TELL_WRITE,          /* get write position */
    ZIP_SOURCE_SUPPORTS,            /* check whether source supports command */
    ZIP_SOURCE_REMOVE,              /* remove file */
    ZIP_SOURCE_RESERVED_1,          /* previously used internally */
    ZIP_SOURCE_BEGIN_WRITE_CLONING, /* like ZIP_SOURCE_BEGIN_WRITE, but keep part of original file */
    ZIP_SOURCE_ACCEPT_EMPTY,        /* whether empty files are valid archives */
    ZIP_SOURCE_GET_FILE_ATTRIBUTES, /* get additional file attributes */
    ZIP_SOURCE_SUPPORTS_REOPEN,     /* allow reading from changed entry */
    ZIP_SOURCE_GET_DOS_TIME         /* get last modification time in DOS format */
};
typedef enum zip_source_cmd zip_source_cmd_t;
objects.description: Enumeration of callback commands used by zip_source callbacks to control reading/writing and query capabilities. The typedef zip_source_cmd_t is the public alias.
Argument payload for ZIP_SOURCE_SEEK and ZIP_SOURCE_SEEK_WRITE commands. Contains offset and whence (SEEK_SET/SEEK_CUR/SEEK_END).
Represents a libzip error with library, system/zlib codes and optional message string. Managed by error APIs; caller may initialize/fini when using standalone instances.
Holds metadata about a zip entry (sizes, times, CRC, methods). Valid bitfield indicates which members are set.
Describes a contiguous memory fragment for building a source from multiple buffers.
Container for additional per-file attributes such as host system, external attributes, and general purpose flags. 'valid' bitmask specifies which fields apply.

functions.name: zip_close
functions.description: Closes the archive, writing changes to disk if necessary. Returns 0 on success or -1 on error.
requirements: zip_t* must be a valid, open archive.
After calling, the zip_t* must not be used again.
Caller should check return value and, on error, consult zip_get_error().

functions.name: zip_delete
functions.description: Deletes an entry from the archive by index (marks for deletion until close).
requirements: zip_t* must be valid.
Index must be in range [0, zip_get_num_entries()).
Check return value for success; on error, use zip_get_error().

functions.name: zip_dir_add
functions.signature: ZIP_EXTERN zip_int64_t zip_dir_add(zip_t *_Nonnull, const char *_Nonnull, zip_flags_t);
functions.description: Adds an empty directory entry to the archive with the given name and flags.
requirements: zip_t* and name must be non-null.
Flags should be from ZIP_FL_* set (e.g., ZIP_FL_OVERWRITE).
Name should follow ZIP directory naming conventions (commonly ending with '/').

functions.name: zip_discard
functions.description: Discards an open archive handle without writing changes (like closing without commit). Frees resources.
requirements: zip_t* must be valid and open.
After calling, the handle must not be used again.

functions.name: zip_get_error
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the archive’s internal error object for detailed error information.
requirements: zip_t* must be valid.
The returned pointer is owned by the archive; do not free it.

functions.name: zip_error_clear
functions.description: Clears the current error state associated with the archive.
requirements: zip_t* must be valid.

functions.name: zip_error_code_zip
functions.description: Returns the libzip error code (ZIP_ER_*) stored in the error object.
requirements: zip_error_t* must be non-null and initialized.

functions.name: zip_error_code_system
functions.description: Returns the associated system error code stored in the error object (errno, zlib code, etc.).
requirements: zip_error_t* must be non-null and initialized.

functions.name: zip_error_fini
functions.description: Finalizes and frees any resources held by a zip_error_t previously initialized.
requirements: zip_error_t* must be non-null and previously initialized with zip_error_init or similar.
Do not use the error object after finalization unless re-initialized.

functions.name: zip_error_init
functions.description: Initializes a zip_error_t to a clean state with no error.
requirements: zip_error_t* must be non-null and writable.
Must be called before using the error object.

functions.name: zip_error_set
functions.description: Sets a zip_error_t to a specific libzip error and system error code.
requirements: Error pointer may be NULL (in which case the call has no effect).
Provide valid libzip error code (ZIP_ER_*) and a system error code consistent with the type.

functions.name: zip_error_set_from_source
functions.description: Copies the current error from a source into the provided error object.
requirements: zip_error_t* must be non-null and writable.
zip_source_t* may be NULL; behavior for NULL is unspecified here.

functions.name: zip_error_system_type

requirements: zip_error_t* must be non-null and initialized.

functions.name: zip_error_to_data

functions.description: Serializes the error object into a buffer (for propagation across APIs). Returns number of bytes written or -1 on error.
requirements: zip_error_t* and output buffer must be non-null.

functions.name: zip_fclose
functions.description: Closes an open file within a zip archive (zip_file_t).
requirements: zip_file_t* must be valid and currently open.
Caller must not use the handle after closing.
Check return value for errors.

functions.name: zip_fdopen
functions.description: Opens a zip archive from an existing file descriptor with flags similar to zip_open. Returns a zip_t* or NULL on error.
requirements: File descriptor must refer to a readable (and possibly writable) ZIP file.
Flags must be a combination of ZIP_CREATE, ZIP_EXCL, ZIP_CHECKCONS, ZIP_TRUNCATE, ZIP_RDONLY as applicable.
Optional error code pointer may be NULL.

requirements: zip_t*, name, and source must be non-null and valid.

functions.name: zip_file_attributes_init
functions.description: Initializes a zip_file_attributes_t to default values and marks valid fields accordingly.
requirements: Pointer must be non-null and writable.

functions.name: zip_file_error_clear

requirements: zip_file_t* must be valid.

Entry index must be valid.

functions.name: zip_file_extra_fields_count
functions.description: Returns the number of extra fields for an entry (local or central per flags), or -1 on error.
requirements: zip_t* must be valid.
Entry index must be valid.
Flags should be ZIP_FL_LOCAL or ZIP_FL_CENTRAL.

functions.name: zip_file_extra_fields_count_by_id
functions.signature: ZIP_EXTERN zip_int16_t zip_file_extra_fields_count_by_id(zip_t *_Nonnull, zip_uint64_t, zip_uint16_t, zip_flags_t);
functions.description: Returns the number of extra fields with a given header ID for an entry (local or central per flags).
requirements: zip_t* must be valid.
Entry index must be valid.
Header ID must be provided.
Flags select local/central.

functions.name: zip_file_extra_field_get

functions.signature: ZIP_EXTERN const zip_uint8_t *_Nullable zip_file_extra_field_get_by_id(zip_t *_Nonnull, zip_uint64_t, zip_uint16_t, zip_uint16_t, zip_uint16_t *_Nullable, zip_flags_t);
functions.description: Retrieves the extra field data matching a header ID and (optionally) selection index. Returns pointer to data or NULL.

functions.signature: ZIP_EXTERN const char *_Nullable zip_file_get_comment(zip_t *_Nonnull, zip_uint64_t, zip_uint32_t *_Nullable, zip_flags_t);
functions.description: Gets the comment string for an entry by index, optionally returning its length. Returns NULL if no comment or on error.
requirements: zip_t* must be valid.

functions.description: Returns a pointer to the error object for a zip_file stream.
requirements: zip_file_t* must be valid.

requirements: zip_t* must be valid.
Index must be valid.

Flags select where to read from (ZIP_FL_LOCAL/ZIP_FL_CENTRAL).

functions.description: Returns non-zero if the zip_file stream supports seeking, 0 otherwise.
requirements: zip_file_t* must be valid.

functions.name: zip_file_rename
functions.signature: ZIP_EXTERN int zip_file_rename(zip_t *_Nonnull, zip_uint64_t, const char *_Nonnull, zip_flags_t);
functions.description: Renames an entry by index to a new name, with flags controlling behavior (e.g., case sensitivity).
requirements: zip_t* and new name must be non-null.
Index must be valid.
Flags must be from ZIP_FL_* set.

functions.name: zip_file_replace

functions.description: Replaces the data of an entry with data from the given source, using flags to control behavior.
requirements: zip_t* and source must be non-null and valid.
Index must be valid.
Flags must be from ZIP_FL_* set.

functions.name: zip_file_set_comment
functions.signature: ZIP_EXTERN int zip_file_set_comment(zip_t *_Nonnull, zip_uint64_t, const char *_Nullable, zip_uint16_t, zip_flags_t);

mtime must be a valid time_t.

import random
import struct
import string

# Generator for an arbitrary binary buffer tailored to libzip fuzz stubs that
# frequently use FUZZ_PARAM_STR as content for zip_source_buffer(_create),
# zip_file_add/replace, and callback-backed sources. We aim to provide valid,
# varied, but plausible contents: small ZIP files, plain text, random bytes,
# repeated patterns, and zero-length buffers. All under 4096 bytes.

ASCII_NAMES = [
    "a.txt", "dir/", "dir/b.txt", "unicodé.txt", "spaced name.txt",
    "nested/dirs/", "nested/dirs/file.bin", "empty", "zeros.bin",
]


def _rand(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _plain_text(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # English-like lines with varying lengths and some non-ASCII sprinkled in
    lines = []
    nlines = r.randint(1, 20)
    for _ in range(nlines):
        length = r.randint(0, 120)
        # Include a range of characters including NUL and high bytes occasionally
        alphabet = string.printable.replace("\x0b", "").replace("\x0c", "")
        s = ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))
        if r.random() < 0.15:
            # inject some binary bytes
            s_bytes = s.encode('utf-8', 'ignore') + _rand(r, r.randint(0, 4))
        else:
            s_bytes = s.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')
        lines.append(s_bytes)
    data = b"\n".join(lines)
    return data[:max_len]


def _patterned(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Repeated patterns (useful for compression paths)
    patterns = [b"A" * r.randint(1, 64), b"0123456789", b"abcd" * 8,
                bytes([r.randrange(256)]) * r.randint(1, 128)]
    base = b"|".join(patterns)
    reps = r.randint(1, max(1, 4096 // max(1, len(base))))
    data = (base * reps)[:max_len]
    return data


def _random_sized(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    size = r.randint(0, max_len)
    return _rand(r, size)


def _minimal_zip_local_file(name: str, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Construct a minimal ZIP with a single stored file (no compression).
    # Local File Header
    # signature, version, flags, method, mtime, mdate, crc32, comp_size, uncomp_size,
    # name_len, extra_len
    import zlib
    name_bytes = name.encode('utf-8')
    crc = zlib.crc32(payload) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    comp = payload  # stored
    lf = []
    lf.append(struct.pack('<I', 0x04034B50))
    lf.append(struct.pack('<HHHHHIIIHH', 20, 0, 0, 0, 0, crc,
                          len(comp), len(payload), len(name_bytes), 0))
    lf.append(name_bytes)
    lf.append(comp)
    local = b''.join(lf)

    # Central Directory Header for the same file
    # Fields: version made by, version needed, flags, method, mtime, mdate,
    # crc32, comp_size, uncomp_size, name len, extra len, comment len,
    # disk start, int attrs, ext attrs, rel offset of local header
    cd = []
    cd.append(struct.pack('<I', 0x02014B50))
    cd.append(struct.pack('<HHHHHHIIIHHHHHII',
                          20,  # version made by
                          20,  # version needed
                          0,   # flags
                          0,   # method (store)
                          0,   # mtime
                          0,   # mdate
                          crc,
                          len(comp),
                          len(payload),
                          len(name_bytes),
                          0,   # extra len
                          0,   # comment len
                          0,   # disk start
                          0,   # internal attrs
                          0,   # external attrs
                          0    # relative offset of local header (we place central after local, so 0)
                          ))
    cd.append(name_bytes)
    central = b''.join(cd)

    # EOCD
    cdir_size = len(central)
    cdir_off = len(local)
    eocd = struct.pack('<IHHHHIIH', 0x06054B50, 0, 0, 1, 1, cdir_size, cdir_off, 0)

    return local + central + eocd


def _tiny_zip_archive(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Build a very small valid ZIP file with 1-2 entries stored method.
    n = 1 if r.random() < 0.7 else 2
    entries = []
    for i in range(n):
        name = r.choice(ASCII_NAMES)
        # ensure files (not directories) for payload entries
        if name.endswith('/'):
            name = name + f"f{i}.txt"
        payload_choice = r.randint(0, 2)
        if payload_choice == 0:
            payload = _plain_text(r, 200)
        elif payload_choice == 1:
            payload = _patterned(r, 200)
        else:
            payload = _random_sized(r, 200)
        entries.append(_minimal_zip_local_file(name, payload))
    data = b''.join(entries)
    return data[:max_len]


def _zero_length() -> bytes:
    return b""


def _with_nuls(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Include embedded NULs around ASCII
    left = _plain_text(r, max_len // 2)
    right = _plain_text(r, max_len // 2)
    nuls = b"\x00" * r.randint(1, 64)
    return (left + nuls + right)[:max_len]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    max_total = 4096
    # Choose a scenario to exercise different code paths:
    #  - 0: zero-length (valid for sources expecting len==0 with NULL or empty data)
    #  - 1: plain text content (good for comments, names-as-bytes, file payload)
    #  - 2: patterned compressible data
    #  - 3: random binary blob
    #  - 4: tiny valid ZIP archive (for zip_open_from_source path)
    #  - 5: ASCII with embedded NULs
    choice = r.randint(0, 5)
    if choice == 0:
        return _zero_length()
    elif choice == 1:
        return _plain_text(r, max_total)
    elif choice == 2:
        return _patterned(r, max_total)
    elif choice == 3:
        return _random_sized(r, max_total)
    elif choice == 4:
        # Build a tiny zip but cap to 3KB to stay small
        return _tiny_zip_archive(r, min(3072, max_total))
    else:
        return _with_nuls(r, max_total)

# This generator produces valid ZIP entry names and small file contents to exercise
# libzip APIs that add and rename entries. Fuzzer stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR to obtain
# both content buffers and entry names. We therefore emit a serialized blob that
# contains multiple length-prefixed strings so the harness can consume them in order.
#
# Format (little-endian):
#   [u16 count]
#   repeat count times:
#       [u16 len] [len bytes data]
#
# Each string will be either:
#   - Entry content: small arbitrary bytes (including binary) up to ~2KB
#   - Entry name: non-empty filename/path strings covering different cases
#
# We craft a sequence that aligns with the target stubs’ needs:
#   For add/file_add we need: content, name.
#   For rename/file_rename we need: new name.
# We provide: content1, name1, content2, name2, newname1, newname2, ...
# The harness will pull strings in order as it needs them; having many ensures
# non-empty values are available and varied.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096
MAX_STR_LEN = 2048

# Some interesting directory and filename components
DIR_NAMES = [
    "",  # will be skipped for root-less paths
    "src",
    "bin",
    "doc",
    "META-INF",
    "..",
    ".",
    "nested",
    "unicodé",  # UTF-8 accent
    "スペース",  # Japanese
]
FILE_BASES = [
    "readme",
    "main",
    "data",
    "a",
    "0",
    "🗂",   # folder emoji
    "コンテンツ",
    "NUL",  # reserved on Windows but allowed as ZIP entry name
    "COM1", # likewise
    "file",
]
EXTS = ["", ".txt", ".c", ".bin", ".json", ".md", ".png", ".zip"]

SPECIAL_NAMES = [
    "dir/",                      # explicit directory entry
    "./relative/path.txt",
    "../up/one/level.bin",
    "spaces in name/read me.md",
    "trailing/space ",
    "leading_space/ _file.txt",
    "double//slash/file.txt",
    "mixed/./and/../nav.txt",
    "unicode/π/ф/名.txt",
]

BINARY_SETS = [
    b"\x00\x01\x02\x03Hello\x00World\xff",
    b"\x78\x9c\x03\x00\x00\x00\x00\x01",  # resembles zlib header
    b"PK\x03\x04minimal",                     # looks like ZIP local header start
]


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _gen_content(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Generate small valid content (any bytes). Mix text and binary.
    choice = rng.randrange(5)
    if choice == 0:
        # ASCII text paragraph
        words = [
            "lorem", "ipsum", "dolor", "sit", "amet", "zip", "libzip",
            "entry", "content", "data", "compress", "store"
        ]
        s = " ".join(rng.choice(words) for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 80)))
        b = s.encode("utf-8")
    elif choice == 1:
        # UTF-8 text with newlines
        lines = [
            "标题: 测试文件", "Описание: пример", "Σχόλιο: δοκιμή",
            "line with emoji 😀", "end"
        ]
        b = ("\n".join(lines) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
    elif choice == 2:
        # Choose from predefined interesting binaries
        b = rng.choice(BINARY_SETS)
    elif choice == 3:
        # Repeated pattern
        pat = rng.choice([b"A", b"\x00", b"\xff\x00", b"ABCD", b"zip!"])
        b = pat * rng.randint(1, 400)
    else:
        # Random bytes up to 1500
        b = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(1, 1500))
    if len(b) > MAX_STR_LEN:
        b = b[:MAX_STR_LEN]
    return b


def _gen_component(rng: random.Random, pool: List[str]) -> str:
    s = rng.choice(pool)
    # Occasionally add random alphanum chunk to diversify
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        extra = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ ") for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 6)))
        s = (s + extra) if s else extra or "x"
    return s


def _gen_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # 30% use a special pre-crafted name
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        name = rng.choice(SPECIAL_NAMES)
    else:
        parts = []
        depth = rng.randint(0, 4)
        for _ in range(depth):
            comp = _gen_component(rng, DIR_NAMES) or "d"
            parts.append(comp)
        base = _gen_component(rng, FILE_BASES) or "f"
        ext = rng.choice(EXTS)
        name = "/".join(p for p in parts if p)
        if name:
            name = name + "/" + base + ext
        else:
            name = base + ext
        # Occasionally force directory entry
        if rng.random() < 0.1:
            name = "/".join(p for p in parts + [base] if p) + "/"
    # Ensure non-empty
    if not name:
        name = "file.txt"
    # Trim to a reasonable length
    if len(name.encode('utf-8')) > 240:
        # Keep last component and a few dirs
        comps = name.split('/')
        name = "/".join((comps[:2] + comps[-2:]))
    return name


def _encode_lp_string(s: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Encode a single string as [u16 len][data]
    if len(s) > 0xFFFF:
        s = s[:0xFFFF]
    return len(s).to_bytes(2, 'little') + s


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Prepare a sequence of alternating contents and names, plus extra rename targets
    entries = []  # list of bytes strings

    num_pairs = rng.randint(2, 6)  # number of content/name pairs
    for _ in range(num_pairs):
        content = _gen_content(rng)
        name = _gen_filename(rng).encode('utf-8', 'surrogatepass')
        entries.append(content)
        entries.append(name)

    # Add several rename targets to ensure availability for rename stubs
    num_renames = rng.randint(2, 6)
    for _ in range(num_renames):
        newname = _gen_filename(rng).encode('utf-8', 'surrogatepass')
        entries.append(newname)

    # Serialize with count header
    # Ensure total size <= MAX_TOTAL
    out = bytearray()
    # Reserve space for count
    out.extend((0).to_bytes(2, 'little'))
    count = 0

    for s in entries:
        chunk = _encode_lp_string(s)
        if len(out) + len(chunk) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out.extend(chunk)
        count += 1

    # Write count at the beginning
    out[0:2] = count.to_bytes(2, 'little')

    return bytes(out)

SEGMENT_CHARS = (

# Produce a random, but valid, directory path ending with a slash
# Try to cover multiple patterns and corner cases.

def _rand_segment(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 32) -> str:
    # Sometimes pick from common list to hit special cases
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        return rng.choice(COMMON_COMPONENTS)
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = "".join(rng.choice(SEGMENT_CHARS) for _ in range(n))
    # Avoid path separators within a single segment; ensure not empty unless control case selected
    s = s.replace("/", "-")
    return s


def _make_variant_paths(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    variants: List[str] = []

    # Basic root-like dir
    variants.append("/")

    # Simple single-segment directories
    for name in ["dir/", "test/", "a/", "./", "../"]:
        variants.append(name)

    # Nested typical dirs
    variants.append("src/include/")
    variants.append("assets/images/")
    variants.append("bin/amd64/")

    # Hidden and dot dirs
    variants.append(".git/")
    variants.append(".config/")

    # Windows-style drive-ish prefix but with POSIX separators (ZIP uses '/'): add slash end
    variants.append("C:/Windows/")

    # Names with spaces and special chars
    variants.append("My Folder (1)/")
    variants.append("sp ace/inner/")

    # Non-ASCII
    variants.append("unicodé/ümlaut/😀/")
    variants.append("重/目录/")

    # Reserved-ish names as components
    variants.append("AUX/NUL/COM1/")

    # Trailing space and dot segments (valid in ZIP names, problematic on some FS)
    variants.append("trail. /dot./")

    # Long multi-level path
    long_segs = ["very" + "-" * 3 + "long", "name", "segment", "x" * 16]
    variants.append("/".join(long_segs) + "/")

    # Empty component collapsing like // or leading ./, ../ patterns
    variants.append("//nested//empty//components//")
    variants.append("././relative/./")
    variants.append("../up/level/")

    # Randomly generated patterns
    for _ in range(8):
        depth = rng.randint(1, 6)
        parts = []
        for i in range(depth):
            seg = _rand_segment(rng)
            parts.append(seg)
        # Occasionally insert empty components to create '//' sequences
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            insert_pos = rng.randrange(0, len(parts) + 1)
            parts.insert(insert_pos, "")
        path = "/".join(parts)
        if not path or path.endswith("/") is False:
            path += "/"
        variants.append(path)

    # Ensure no variant exceeds size limit badly; trim conservatively keeping '/'
    trimmed: List[str] = []
    for v in variants:
        b = v.encode("utf-8", errors="surrogatepass")
        if len(b) > MAX_TOTAL_SIZE:
            # Keep tail to preserve structure and ending slash
            enc = b[: MAX_TOTAL_SIZE - 1]
            # Make sure ends with '/'
            if not enc.endswith(b"/"):
                enc = enc.rstrip(b"/") + b"/"
            v = enc.decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
        trimmed.append(v)

    return trimmed


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a pool of interesting directory names
    paths = _make_variant_paths(rng)

    # Choose a strategy: single dir name or multiple concatenated names separated by NUL
    # FUZZ harness often reads one string; however, providing multiple NUL-separated
    # candidates lets the fuzzer pick different slices when it mutates offsets.
    strategy = rng.random()

    if strategy < 0.7:
        chosen = rng.choice(paths)
        out = chosen.encode("utf-8", errors="surrogatepass")
    else:
        count = rng.randint(2, min(8, len(paths)))
        chosen = rng.sample(paths, count)
        # Use NUL separators to allow distinct extraction, ensure final ends with '/'
        out = b"\x00".join(s.encode("utf-8", errors="surrogatepass") for s in chosen)

    # Ensure non-empty and size-limited
    if not out:
        out = b"/"
    if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL_SIZE:
        out = out[:MAX_TOTAL_SIZE]
        # try to end with '/' or NUL to keep last token clean
        if out[-1:] not in (b"/", b"\x00"):
            out = out.rstrip(b"/")
            if not out.endswith(b"/"):
                out += b"/"

    return out

# Target data type: arbitrary text string used for ZIP comments. Constraints:
# - Length 0..65535 (uint16 max) for comment setters
# - May be UTF-8 or other encodings; binary accepted
# - Fuzzer uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR and sometimes unsigned ints. Our single buffer
#   will be consumed by the harness to feed both. We'll craft a compact container
#   that includes multiple candidate strings and integers.
#
# Strategy:
# - Build a small container format with multiple strings separated by length prefixes so
#   FUZZ_PARAM_STR can slice substrings from the byte stream.
# - Include diverse strings: ASCII, UTF-8 with multi-byte, variable sizes, some binary with NULs.
# - Keep total <= 4096 bytes.
# - Also include 4-byte little-endian integers as short entries to yield varied values for
#   FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) uses in the harness.
#
# Container layout (all concatenated):
#   [magic b"ZCMT"]
#   [u16 count_le]
#   Repeated for each entry:
#     [u16 length_le]
#     [bytes payload of that length]

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _u16(n: int) -> bytes:
    return int(n & 0xFFFF).to_bytes(2, 'little')

def _u32(n: int) -> bytes:
    return int(n & 0xFFFFFFFF).to_bytes(4, 'little')

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    l = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " -_./:\\()[]{}!@#$%^&*?,;+'\""
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(chars) for _ in range(l))
    return s.encode('utf-8')

def _utf8_samples() -> List[bytes]:
    return [
        "こんにちは世界".encode('utf-8'),
        "Привет мир".encode('utf-8'),
        "مرحبا بالعالم".encode('utf-8'),
        "γειά σου κόσμε".encode('utf-8'),
        "안녕하세요 세계".encode('utf-8'),
        "🙂🚀📦 ZIPコメント".encode('utf-8'),
    ]

def _binary_chunk(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    # Include NULs and high bytes
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(length))

def _make_comment_of_size(rng: random.Random, size: int) -> bytes:
    # Create a comment exactly of requested size with a mix of text and binary
    if size == 0:
        return b""
    parts = []
    remaining = size
    # Start with UTF-8 label when possible
    prefix = "CMT: ".encode('utf-8')
    if remaining >= len(prefix) + 1:
        parts.append(prefix)
        remaining -= len(prefix)
    # Fill rest with ASCII and binary mix
    flip = False
    while remaining > 0:
        chunk = min(remaining, 64)
        if not flip:
            data = _rand_ascii(rng, chunk, chunk)
        else:
            data = _binary_chunk(rng, chunk)
        flip = not flip
        if len(data) > remaining:
            data = data[:remaining]
        parts.append(data)
        remaining -= len(data)
    return b''.join(parts)[:size]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    entries: List[bytes] = []

    # Special length edge cases for ZIP comments (we keep sizes small for overall budget)
    entries.append(b"")                    # empty -> clear comment
    entries.append(b"a")                   # length 1
    entries.append(_make_comment_of_size(rng, 256))
    entries.append(_make_comment_of_size(rng, 1024))

    # A longer sample within budget
    long_sample = _rand_ascii(rng, 1500, 2000)
    entries.append(long_sample)

    # UTF-8 samples
    entries.extend(_utf8_samples())

    # Path-like and directory names (comments often include filenames)
    path_samples = [
        b"dir/",
        b"folder/subfolder/",
        b"file.txt",
        b"path/with spaces/and-unicode-\x1f600",  # include a control+hex sequence
    ]
    entries.extend(path_samples)

    # Binary payloads with NULs
    entries.append(b"\x00\x00\x00\x00")
    entries.append(b"\xFF\xFE\xFD\xFC\x00BIN\x00DATA\x00")

    # Typical comment texts
    entries.append(b"This is an archive comment.")
    entries.append(b"Entry-specific comment: OK")
    entries.append(b"ZIP\nMulti-line\nComment\nEnd")

    # Additional random strings
    for _ in range(5):
        entries.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 5, 200))

    # Include integers as 4-byte little-endian values for varied flag/int consumption
    int_values = [
        0, 1, 2, 3, 0xFFFFFFFF,
        65535, 32768, 123456789, 0x80000000, 0x7FFFFFFF,
        rng.getrandbits(32), rng.getrandbits(32), rng.getrandbits(32)
    ]
    for v in int_values:
        entries.append(_u32(v))

    # Build container
    out = bytearray()
    out.extend(b"ZCMT")
    count_pos = len(out)
    out.extend(_u16(0))  # placeholder for count

    count = 0
    for e in entries:
        if len(e) > 65535:
            e = e[:65535]
        rec = _u16(len(e)) + e
        if len(out) + len(rec) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out.extend(rec)
        count += 1

    # Update count
    out[count_pos:count_pos+2] = _u16(count)

    return bytes(out)

        0x00000008,
        0x00000100,
        0x00001000,
        0x00010000,
        0x40000000,

        0xFFFFFFFF,
    ]


def _embed_nulls(s: bytes, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    if not s:
        return s
    s = bytearray(s)
    # Insert a few NULs at random positions to test handling of embedded zeros.
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        pos = rng.randrange(0, len(s))
        s[pos] = 0
    return bytes(s)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    out = bytearray()

    # 1) Provide a sequence of unsigned ints for indices, method selection, and flags
    # We interleave method-bias ints and flag patterns multiple times.
    for v in _method_bias_values():
        out += _tlv_uint(v)
    for v in _flag_patterns():
        out += _tlv_uint(v)

    # Additional random ints to diversify modulo-based choices and indices.
    for _ in range(10):
        out += _tlv_uint(rng.getrandbits(32))

    # 2) Provide password strings
    # - common passwords
    for s in _common_passwords():
        out += _tlv_str(s.encode('utf-8'))

    # - UTF-8 variants
    for s in _utf8_variants():
        out += _tlv_str(s.encode('utf-8'))

    # - Random ASCII length 1..32
    for _ in range(5):
        s = _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 32).encode('utf-8')
        out += _tlv_str(s)

    # - High-entropy random bytes lengths 8..32
    for _ in range(5):
        s = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(8, 32))
        out += _tlv_str(s)

    # - Boundary: long password close to 128 bytes, exactly 128, and 127
    long1 = _rand_bytes(rng, 127)
    long2 = _rand_bytes(rng, 128)
    out += _tlv_str(long1)
    out += _tlv_str(long2)

    # - Password with embedded NULs
    nul_bytes = _embed_nulls(b"Null\x00Inside\x00Pwd" + _rand_bytes(rng, 10), rng)
    out += _tlv_str(nul_bytes)

    # - Repeated patterns
    out += _tlv_str(b"AAAAAA")
    out += _tlv_str(b"\x00" * 16)  # all zeros

    # Ensure total size <= 4096 bytes
    if len(out) > 4096:
        out = out[:4096]

    return bytes(out)

import io
import os
import random
import struct
import time
from typing import List, Tuple
import binascii

# Generates valid ZIP archives (bytes) suitable for libzip fuzzers that open files/FILE*.
# Ensures validity and variety while keeping size <= 4096 bytes.


def dos_time_date(ts: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    t = time.localtime(ts)
    dos_time = ((t.tm_hour & 0x1F) << 11) | ((t.tm_min & 0x3F) << 5) | ((t.tm_sec // 2) & 0x1F)
    year = max(1980, min(2107, t.tm_year))
    dos_date = (((year - 1980) & 0x7F) << 9) | (((t.tm_mon) & 0x0F) << 5) | (t.tm_mday & 0x1F)
    return dos_time, dos_date


class ZipBuilder:
    def __init__(self):
        self.buf = io.BytesIO()
        self.central = io.BytesIO()
        self.records = 0
        self.local_offsets: List[int] = []

    def add_file(
        self,
        name: bytes,
        data: bytes,
        use_data_descriptor: bool,
        add_extra: bool,
        add_comment: bool,
        method_store: bool,
        ext_attr: int,
        host_system: int,
        gp_flags_extra: int,
        dos_ts: int,
    ) -> None:
        name_len = len(name)
        extra = b""
        if add_extra:
            payload1 = os.urandom(4)
            ef1 = struct.pack("<HH", 0xCAFE, len(payload1)) + payload1
            mtime = int(dos_ts)
            ef2 = struct.pack("<HHB", 0x5455, 1 + 4, 0x01) + struct.pack("<I", mtime)
            extra = ef1 + ef2
        file_comment = b""
        if add_comment:
            file_comment = b"cmt:" + binascii.hexlify(os.urandom(4))
        # Use stored method to avoid compression; method is 0
        method = 0 if method_store else 0
        gp_flags = 0
        if use_data_descriptor:
            gp_flags |= 1 << 3
        gp_flags |= (gp_flags_extra & ((1 << 11) | (1 << 0)))
        dost, dosd = dos_time_date(dos_ts)
        comp_data = data
        crc = binascii.crc32(data) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        comp_size = len(comp_data)
        uncomp_size = len(data)
        self.local_offsets.append(self.buf.tell())
        if use_data_descriptor:
            l_crc = 0
            l_comp = 0
            l_uncomp = 0
        else:
            l_crc = crc
            l_comp = comp_size
            l_uncomp = uncomp_size
        # Local file header
        local_hdr = struct.pack(
            "<IHHHHHIIIHH",
            0x04034B50,
            20,
            gp_flags,
            method,
            dost,
            dosd,
            l_crc,
            l_comp,
            l_uncomp,
            name_len,
            len(extra),
        )
        self.buf.write(local_hdr)
        self.buf.write(name)
        self.buf.write(extra)
        self.buf.write(comp_data)
        if use_data_descriptor:
            dd = struct.pack("<IIII", 0x08074B50, crc, comp_size, uncomp_size)
            self.buf.write(dd)
        # Central directory header
        # Layout fields (in order):
        # signature, ver_made, ver_needed, flags, method, time, date, crc,
        # csize, usize, name_len, extra_len, comment_len, disk, int_attr,
        # ext_attr, local_header_offset
        cen_hdr = struct.pack(
            "<I H H H H H H I I I H H H H H I I",
            0x02014B50,
            (host_system << 8) | 20,
            20,
            gp_flags,
            method,
            dost,
            dosd,
            crc,
            comp_size,
            uncomp_size,
            name_len,
            len(extra),
            len(file_comment),
            0,  # disk number start
            0,  # internal file attributes
            ext_attr,  # external file attributes
            self.local_offsets[-1],  # relative offset of local header
        )
        self.central.write(cen_hdr)
        self.central.write(name)
        self.central.write(extra)
        self.central.write(file_comment)
        self.records += 1

    def finish(self, archive_comment: bytes) -> bytes:
        cd_start = self.buf.tell()
        cd_data = self.central.getvalue()
        self.buf.write(cd_data)
        cd_size = len(cd_data)
        eocd = struct.pack(
            "<IHHHHIIH",
            0x06054B50,
            0,
            0,
            self.records,
            self.records,
            cd_size,
            cd_start,
            len(archive_comment),
        )
        self.buf.write(eocd)
        self.buf.write(archive_comment)
        return self.buf.getvalue()


def _rand_filename(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    choices = [
        b"a.txt",
        b"dir/",
        b"dir/b.bin",
        b"unicodename.txt",
        b"empty",
        b"path/with/spaces name.dat",
    ]
    return rng.choice(choices)


def _rand_data(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    modes = ["zeros", "ascii", "random", "pattern"]
    mode = rng.choice(modes)
    length = rng.randint(0, max_len)
    if mode == "zeros":
        return b"\x00" * length
    if mode == "ascii":
        base = b"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. "
        return (base * ((length // len(base)) + 1))[:length]
    if mode == "pattern":
        pat = b"\x00\xFF\xAA\x55"
        return (pat * ((length // len(pat)) + 1))[:length]
    return rng.randbytes(length)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    zb = ZipBuilder()

    archive_comment = b""
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        archive_comment = (b"arch:" + binascii.hexlify(rng.randbytes(rng.randint(0, 12))))[:64]

    count = rng.randint(1, 4)
    now = int(time.time())

    for _ in range(count):
        name = _rand_filename(rng)
        is_dir = name.endswith(b"/")
        max_data = 256 if not is_dir else 0
        data = b"" if is_dir else _rand_data(rng, max_len=max_data)
        use_dd = (rng.random() < 0.4) and (not is_dir)
        add_extra = rng.random() < 0.6
        add_comment = rng.random() < 0.4
        method_store = True
        dos_attr = 0x10 if is_dir else 0x20
        unix_perms = 0o100644 if not is_dir else 0o040755
        ext_attr = (unix_perms << 16) | dos_attr
        host_system = rng.choice([0, 3, 10, 19])
        gp_flags_extra = 0
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            gp_flags_extra |= (1 << 11)
        ts = now - rng.randint(0, 60 * 60 * 24 * 365)
        zb.add_file(
            name=name,
            data=data,
            use_data_descriptor=use_dd,
            add_extra=add_extra,
            add_comment=add_comment,
            method_store=method_store,
            ext_attr=ext_attr,
            host_system=host_system,
            gp_flags_extra=gp_flags_extra,
            dos_ts=ts,
        )

    zip_bytes = zb.finish(archive_comment=archive_comment)
    if len(zip_bytes) > 4096:
        rng = random.Random(seed ^ 0xA5A5)
        zb2 = ZipBuilder()
        count2 = max(1, min(3, count))
        for _ in range(count2):
            name = _rand_filename(rng)
            is_dir = name.endswith(b"/")
            max_data = 64 if not is_dir else 0
            data = b"" if is_dir else _rand_data(rng, max_len=max_data)
            use_dd = False
            add_extra = rng.random() < 0.3
            add_comment = False
            method_store = True
            dos_attr = 0x10 if is_dir else 0x20
            unix_perms = 0o100644 if not is_dir else 0o040755
            ext_attr = (unix_perms << 16) | dos_attr
            host_system = 3
            gp_flags_extra = 0
            ts = int(time.time())
            zb2.add_file(
                name,
                data,
                use_dd,
                add_extra,
                add_comment,
                method_store,
                ext_attr,
                host_system,
                gp_flags_extra,
                ts,
            )
        zip_bytes = zb2.finish(archive_comment=b"")
    return zip_bytes
